nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-01.title: Set up an equation
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-01.body:
Let the number be $x$. Then $x+1.2=1.2x$, so $1.2=0.2x$ and $x=6$. Check: $6+1.2=7.2=6\cdot1.2$.

**Answer: 6**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-02.title: Cycles of units digits
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-02.body:
Powers of $3$ end in $3,9,7,1$ (cycle of 4); since $4\mid 88$, $3^{88}$ ends in $1$. Powers of $7$ end in $7,9,3,1$; since $87\equiv3\pmod4$, $7^{87}$ ends in $3$. The product ends in $1\cdot3=3$.

**Answer: 3**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-02.title: Pair the factors
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-02.body:
$3^{88}\cdot7^{87}=21^{87}\cdot3$. Every power of $21$ ends in $1$, so the number ends in $3$.

**Answer: 3**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-03.title: Drop altitudes
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-03.body:
The bases are $5$ and $13$ and the legs are $7$. Dropping altitudes from the ends of the short base cuts off segments of $\frac{13-5}{2}=4$ on the long base, so the height is $\sqrt{49-16}=\sqrt{33}$. A diagonal spans a horizontal distance $13-4=9$, so its length is $\sqrt{33+81}=\sqrt{114}$.

**Answer: $\sqrt{114}$**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-03.title: Ptolemy
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-03.body:
An isosceles trapezoid is cyclic, so Ptolemy's theorem gives $d^2=5\cdot13+7\cdot7=114$, and $d=\sqrt{114}$.

**Answer: $\sqrt{114}$**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-04.title: Digit sum
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-04.body:
The digit sum is $3+1+6+5+2+8+4+9+A+7+6+3+4=58+A$. It must be a multiple of $9$, and with $0\le A\le9$ the only choice is $58+5=63$. So $A=5$.

**Answer: 5**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-05.title: Next multiple of 180
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-05.body:
The angle sum of an $n$-gon is $(n-2)\cdot180^\circ$, and the missing angle is strictly between $0^\circ$ and $180^\circ$ (convex). The only multiple of $180$ between $1930$ and $2110$ is $1980$, so the missing angle is $50^\circ$ and $(n-2)180=1980$ gives $n=13$.

**Answer: 13**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-06.title: Quadratic in |x|
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-06.body:
Let $t=|x|\ge0$. Then $t^2+t-42=(t+7)(t-6)=0$, so $t=6$ (the root $-7$ is impossible for an absolute value). Hence $|x|=6$ and $x=6$ or $x=-6$.

**Answer: $x=\pm6$**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-08.title: Six equilateral triangles
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-08.body:
The hexagon splits into $6$ equilateral triangles of side $8$, each with area $\frac{\sqrt3}{4}\cdot64=16\sqrt3$. Total: $96\sqrt3$.

**Answer: $96\sqrt3$**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-09.title: Rotations and flips
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-09.body:
There are $6!=720$ linear orders. Each bracelet arrangement corresponds to $6$ rotations and $2$ directions (a bracelet can be turned over), so the count is $\frac{720}{12}=60$.

**Answer: 60**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-10.title: Count factors of 5
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-10.body:
Each trailing zero needs a factor $10=2\cdot5$, and factors of $2$ are plentiful, so count factors of $5$: $\left\lfloor\frac{50}{5}\right\rfloor+\left\lfloor\frac{50}{25}\right\rfloor=10+2=12$.

**Answer: 12**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-11.title: Area two ways
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-11.body:
The right triangle has legs $4$ and $3$, area $6$, and hypotenuse $BC=5$. If $h$ is the altitude to $BC$, then $\frac12\cdot5\cdot h=6$, so $h=\frac{12}{5}$.

**Answer: $\frac{12}{5}$**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-11.title: Distance to a line
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-11.body:
Line $BC$ is $3x+4y=12$. The distance from $(0,0)$ is $\frac{|0+0-12|}{\sqrt{9+16}}=\frac{12}{5}$.

**Answer: $\frac{12}{5}$**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-12.title: Factor
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-12.body:
$\sin2x-\cos x=2\sin x\cos x-\cos x=\cos x(2\sin x-1)$. On $[0^\circ,90^\circ]$, $\cos x\ge0$, with equality only at $90^\circ$. So the inequality holds when $2\sin x-1\ge0$, i.e. $x\ge30^\circ$, and also at $x=90^\circ$ (already included). The solution is $30^\circ\le x\le90^\circ$.

**Answer: $30^\circ\le x\le 90^\circ$**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-13.title: It is a rectangle
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-13.body:
Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add to $180^\circ$, and in a parallelogram they are equal, so all angles are $90^\circ$: $ABCD$ is a rectangle. Its diagonal $\sqrt{16+36}=\sqrt{52}=2\sqrt{13}$ is a diameter, so the radius is $\sqrt{13}$.

**Answer: $\sqrt{13}$**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-14.title: Total time
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-14.body:
Let the one-way distance be $d$. At $40$ mph each way he would use $\frac{2d}{40}=\frac{d}{20}$ hours in all. The outbound trip takes $\frac{d}{30}$, leaving $\frac d{20}-\frac d{30}=\frac{d}{60}$ for the return. So he must drive at $60$ mph.

**Answer: 60 mph**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-14.title: Pick a distance
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-14.body:
Take $d=120$ miles. The planned time is $3+3=6$ hours; going out takes $4$ hours, so $120$ miles must be covered in $2$ hours: $60$ mph.

**Answer: 60 mph**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-15.title: Remove the core
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-15.body:
There are $8^3=512$ unit cubes. The unpainted ones form the inner $6\times6\times6$ block of $216$ cubes. So $512-216=296$ have at least one painted face.

**Answer: 296**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-16.title: Equation
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-16.body:
The first four tests total $320$. If the fifth mark is $t$, then $t=\frac{320+t}{5}-16$, so $5t=320+t-80$, $4t=240$, $t=60$. (Check: average $\frac{380}{5}=76=60+16$.)

**Answer: 60**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-17.title: Binomial theorem
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-17.body:
The terms are $\binom6k x^{6-k}(-2)^k$ for $k=0,\dots,6$. The sixth term has $k=5$: $\binom65(-2)^5x=6\cdot(-32)x=-192x$.

**Answer: $-192$**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-18.title: Two cones
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-18.body:
The diagonal has length $6\sqrt2$. The solid is two cones joined at their bases; each has height $3\sqrt2$ (half the diagonal) and base radius $3\sqrt2$ (the distance from the other two vertices to the diagonal). Volume:
$$2\cdot\frac13\pi(3\sqrt2)^2(3\sqrt2)=2\cdot\frac13\pi\cdot18\cdot3\sqrt2=36\sqrt2\,\pi.$$

**Answer: $36\pi\sqrt2$**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-19.title: Repeating block
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-19.body:
$\frac1{14}=0.0\overline{714285}$. After the first digit $0$, the block $714285$ repeats from digit $2$ on. Digit $1991$ is at position $1991-1=1990$ in the repeating part, and $1990=6\cdot331+4$, so it is the $4$th digit of $714285$, namely $2$.

**Answer: 2**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-20.title: Binomial probability
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-20.body:
A single roll is less than $3$ (a $1$ or $2$) with probability $\frac13$. Exactly $5$ such rolls out of $6$: $\binom65\left(\frac13\right)^5\frac23=6\cdot\frac{2}{729}=\frac{4}{243}$.

**Answer: $\frac{4}{243}$**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-22.title: Work fractions
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-22.body:
Mary paints $\frac1{10}$ of the room per hour, so in her $6$ hours she paints $\frac6{10}$. John paints the other $\frac4{10}$ in $2$ hours, i.e. $\frac15$ per hour. Alone he needs $5$ hours.

**Answer: 5 hours**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-23.title: Choose pairs
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-23.body:
Each handshake is a pair of people: $\binom{20}{2}=\frac{20\cdot19}{2}=190$.

**Answer: 190**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-24.title: Maximize a quadratic
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-24.body:
After $k$ nickel increases the fare is $1+0.05k$ dollars and there are $500-10k$ riders. Revenue $R=(1+0.05k)(500-10k)=0.05(20+k)\cdot10(50-k)=0.5(20+k)(50-k)$, which is proportional to $(20+k)(50-k)$. This parabola has roots $k=-20$ and $k=50$, so it peaks halfway, at $k=15$. The fare is $1+0.75=\$1.75$ (revenue $1.75\cdot350=\$612.50$).

**Answer: \$1.75**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-25.title: Equation
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-25.body:
Let the daughter be $d$, so David is $5d$. Then $5d+21=2(d+21)$, giving $3d=21$, $d=7$, and David is $35$.

**Answer: 35**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-26.title: The overlap is an isosceles triangle
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-26.body:
Let the common hypotenuse be $AB=6$. For a partial overlap the triangles lie on the same side of $AB$ with their $30^\circ$ angles at opposite ends: one has $30^\circ$ at $A$, the other $30^\circ$ at $B$. The common region is the triangle with base $AB$ and base angles $30^\circ$ and $30^\circ$. Its height is $3\tan30^\circ=\sqrt3$, so its area is $\frac12\cdot6\cdot\sqrt3=3\sqrt3$.

**Answer: $3\sqrt3$**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-27.title: Unfold two faces
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-27.body:
The fly must walk on the surfaces. Unfold the floor and an adjacent wall into a $10\times20$ rectangle; the corners become opposite corners of this rectangle, and the straight path has length $\sqrt{10^2+20^2}=10\sqrt5$.

**Answer: $10\sqrt5$ feet**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-29.title: Combine the equations
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-29.body:
With prices $s,d,e$: $7s+5d+e=32$ and $10s+7d+e=45$. Three times the first minus twice the second gives $(21-20)s+(15-14)d+(3-2)e=96-90$, i.e. $s+d+e=6$.

**Answer: \$6**

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-30.title: Product formula
nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-30.body:
Let $D=\cos36^\circ-\cos72^\circ$. Using $\cos A-\cos B=-2\sin\frac{A+B}2\sin\frac{A-B}2$: $D=2\sin54^\circ\sin18^\circ=2\cos36^\circ\sin18^\circ$. Multiply by $\cos18^\circ$: $D\cos18^\circ=\cos36^\circ\sin36^\circ=\frac12\sin72^\circ=\frac12\cos18^\circ$, so $D=\frac12$. Hence $\cos72^\circ-\cos36^\circ=-\frac12$.

**Answer: $-\frac12$**
